title: Improved image quality in CT pulmonary angiography using deep learning-based image reconstruction.
summary: a retrospective single-center study reconstructed CTPA images from 220 patients (40 PE positive) using FBP, ASiR-V and three DLIR strengths. Deep-learning reconstruction reduced image noise and improved objective and radiologist-rated image quality versus comparators; report this as an imaging-quality result only, not diagnostic outcome or dose-reduction evidence. First publisher version date is 2024-01-30.
ai_technology: DLIR reconstructions at three strengths are compared with FBP and iterative ASiR-V for the same CTPA examinations.
organization: Not stated in the abstract reviewed

evidence.tested: In 220 consecutive patients, including 40 PE-positive exams, DLIR reduced noise and improved objective image-quality metrics; claim is image quality, not diagnostic accuracy.
evidence.unknown: Paired reconstructions from one retrospective single-center cohort were statistically compared; radiologist-rated image quality and objective measures provide within-cohort validation, with no prospective outcome or multi-center validation.
